chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Ali ibn Ri'ab from Abu Hamzah said: I heard Jabir al-Ansari narrating, saying:

We were sitting with the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), and we mentioned women and the superiority of some of them over others. So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Shall I not inform you?' We said: 'Yes, O Messenger of Allah, so inform us.' He said: 'Indeed, among the best of your women is the fertile, the affectionate, the modest, the respected among her family, the humble with her husband, the unveiled (open) with her spouse, the chaste against others, the one who hears his word and obeys his command, and when he is alone with her, she yields to him what he desires from her, and she does not yield to him with the yielding of a man.'

Then he said: 'Shall I not inform you of the worst of your women?' They said: 'Yes.' He said: 'Indeed, among the worst of your women is the humble among her family, the respected with her husband, the barren, the resentful, the one who does not refrain from ugliness, the unveiled when her husband is absent from her, the chaste with him when he is present, the one who does not hear his word nor obey his command, and when her husband is alone with her, she refuses him with the refusal of the stubborn beast when being mounted, and she does not accept his excuse nor forgive his sin.'

Then he said: 'Shall I not inform you of the best of your men?' We said: 'Yes.' He said: 'Indeed, among the best of your men is the pious, the pure, the generous, the two-handed (capable), the sound of the two eyes, the righteous to his parents, and the one who does not force his dependents to rely on others.'

Then he said: 'Shall I not inform you of the worst of your men?' We said: 'Yes.' He said: 'Indeed, among the worst of your men is the show-off, the obscene, the one who eats alone, the one who withholds his provision, the one who strikes his family and his servant, the stingy, the one who forces his dependents to rely on others, the disobedient to his parents.'

key_terms.اَلْفَاحِشَ: Obscene, vulgar in speech or action

ai.seo_question: What are the characteristics of the best and worst women and men according to this hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* within the chapter on choosing spouses, this hadith provides a comprehensive typology of marital virtues and vices, emphasizing the interplay between domestic modesty (*al-satirah*) and conjugal availability. It reflects the Shia scholarly focus on balancing spiritual piety with practical household harmony, where the wife’s obedience is paired with the husband’s provision and the man’s piety is measured by his generosity and filial duty.
